summary: CropShield is a satellite-data-based agricultural decision-support prototype designed to help farmers understand environmental conditions that may affect crop health. It addresses the challenge of adapting agriculture to changing environmental conditions by integrating NASA POWER weather data, MODIS vegetation indices (NDVI), and SMAP soil moisture estimates through Google Earth Engine. The platform presents temperature, humidity, rainfall, vegetation greenness, and soil moisture information in a simple dashboard and identifies potential environmental stress indicators. CropShield aims to make Earth observation data more understandable and accessible for agricultural monitoring and decision-making. It provides preliminary environmental assessments, not confirmed crop disease diagnoses. In the future, we aim to improve crop-specific assessments, historical comparisons, and local validation to support more informed agricultural decisions.
details:
CropShield is an agricultural decision-support prototype that helps farmers understand environmental conditions affecting crop health using NASA satellite data. It integrates NASA POWER weather data, MODIS NDVI, and SMAP soil moisture through Google Earth Engine. The platform displays temperature, humidity, rainfall, vegetation greenness, and soil moisture in a simple dashboard and provides preliminary environmental stress indicators to support agricultural decisions.

CropShield aims to make NASA Earth observation data more understandable and accessible for farmers, helping them make more informed decisions and adapt to changing environmental conditions. Our project was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Python, Flask, and Google Earth Engine. We used modern web technologies to create an interactive and user-friendly platform.

The creative aspect of CropShield is combining multiple NASA datasets into one simple agricultural monitoring platform. Our team considered data availability, accessibility, usability, and scientific limitations. The current prototype provides environmental assessments, not confirmed crop disease diagnoses.
